newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close weaker after New York dives.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close weaker after New York dives.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks were dragged down by a sharp drop on Wall Street despite high flying golds and firmer retail issues. * Toronto market posts heaviest trading ever.
Toronto stocks were dragged down to close weaker in its heaviest trading to date on Thursday by a last minute sell-off on New York.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index lost 43.79 points to settle at 6205.07, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 92.75 points to reach 6927.38.
Canada's largest equities market also posted its heaviest trading session and highest value ever, with 169.4 million shares traded worth C$2.97 billion.
Despite the drop the 300 index did not cross the key mark of 6175 points, said portfolio consultant Ron Meisels.
"We're still actually very much above the break-out level," Meisels said.
Declining stocks edged out advancing ones 518 to 515 while 268 traded flat.
Toronto's losses were checked by a soaring gold group, which rocketed 3.23 percent on surging bullion price on COMEX. April gold closed $5.00 higher an ounce at $352.70.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-indices lost ground except for golds and retail. Consumer products led losses, followed by banks, oils and utilities.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Bre-X Minerals Ltd continued to be active, rising 1.20 to 22.70 on 6.7 million shares. Shareholders were cheered by Bre-X's statement on Wednesday that its huge Busang discovery contains 200 million ounces of gold.
Minorca Resources Inc, which holds a small stake in the profits, rose 1.05 to 6.45 in heavy dealings.

* United Grain Growers Ltd shares rose 1.75 to 14.25 in light trading after news that two grain handling rivals, Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators, said they will make a C$13.75 a share offer for all UGG shares.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100))
